name: Tailscale

fields.name: tailnet
fields.label: Tailnet (use a dash for the default)

auth.keyHelp: Generate an access token (1 to 90 days); it can do everything its owner can, so for read-only use create an OAuth client with the all:read scope under Trust credentials instead.

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Read from the API's own published OpenAPI schema (the file behind tailscale.com/api, which says its spec is unstable and may change) plus the OAuth and trust credential pages. Base URL https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2. Auth: an API access token goes either as Authorization: Bearer <token> or as the username of HTTP Basic with a blank password; tokens carry the prefix tskey-api-. The {tailnet} path value can be a dash, which means the default tailnet of the token; otherwise the Tailnet ID from General Settings (older legacy tailnet names still work for tailnets made before Oct 2025). The API does not paginate. Test call: GET /tailnet/-/devices; the schema names no whoami endpoint, so who is null. NO READ-ONLY API ACCESS TOKEN EXISTS: the docs say access tokens have the same permissions as the user who owns them and can be set to expire in 1 to 90 days, so a key from the Keys page is full access. The way to get read-only is a trust credential: an OAuth client created at https://console.tailscale.com/admin/settings/trust-credentials (Owner, Admin, Network admin or IT admin only; pick Read or Write per area, copy the client secret at once because it cannot be shown again) with scope all:read, which the trust credentials page says grants read access to the whole tailnet including future APIs. Exchange it at POST https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2/oauth/token with form fields client_id and client_secret (the page example omits grant_type; it calls the flow OAuth 2.0 client credentials); the response has access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600 and scope, and the lifetime cannot be changed, so a new token is needed about hourly. The auth.altAuth block is an extra beyond FORMAT.md for this path, because signIn cannot describe a client credentials exchange. Finer read scopes exist: devices:core:read, devices:routes:read, users:read, dns:read, policy_file:read, account_settings:read and others. The schema lists devices:core:read for list/get device, users:read for list users, devices:routes:read for routes, devices:core for authorize and expire (the write actions need a write token or scope, so a read-only credential will refuse them). The schema printed no OAuth scope line for the DNS endpoints that I could match, and it shows policy_file:read for the tailnet settings call, which looks odd, so use all:read rather than trying to pick scopes one by one. Official MCP: Tailscale publishes a remote MCP server at https://tailscale.mcp.kapa.ai/ (OAuth sign-in in the browser), but its docs say it only searches Tailscale documentation and does not manage a tailnet, so mcp is null here; it is not an account connection. I found no official Tailscale MCP server that reads or changes a tailnet; the ones that came up in search were third-party. Authorizing a device and expiring a device key are left out on purpose: the Hub offers no change action on this service for now.
